thread.title: Malibu Wildfire: Bryson Fire Burns 102 Acres, Evacuations Ordered
thread.title_full: Malibu Wildfire: Bryson Fire Burns 102 Acres, Evacuations Ordered

author: Newsweek
title: Malibu Wildfire: Bryson Fire Burns 102 Acres, Evacuations Ordered
text:
The Bryson Fire in Malibu has burned 102 acres, prompting evacuations and power shutoffs. Santa Ana winds are expected to strengthen overnight, with gusts up to 60 mph.
A wildfire named the Bryson Fire broke out in Malibu, California, on Thursday evening, burning 102 acres within about two hours, according to Cal Fire. The wind-driven blaze was reported around 5 p.m. local time near the intersection of Mulholland Highway and Encinal Canyon Road. Evacuation orders and warnings have been issued as dangerous Santa Ana wind conditions persist. The Los Angeles County Fire Department issued an evacuation order for the Encinal Canyon area of Malibu, with evacuation warnings extending down to the beaches.
Malibu Fire Spread and Evacuation Orders
The Bryson Fire spread rapidly due to strong winds. Winds are expected to strengthen overnight, with gusts of 50 to 60 mph possible, according to the National Weather Service in Los Angeles. A red flag warning was in effect across parts of Southern California on Thursday because of strong winds and high temperatures.
As of Thursday night, Southern California Edison implemented public safety power shutoffs for more than 60,000 customers in Los Angeles and Ventura Counties due to heightened wildfire risk. The utility posted on X that during dangerous fire weather, it may temporarily shut off power in targeted areas to reduce wildfire risk and protect customers and communities.
State and Local Response to the Fire
Governor Gavin Newsom has been briefed on the Bryson Fire, and the California Governor's Office of Emergency Services is coordinating support and resources to assist local first responders, according to Newsom's office on X. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said her office is closely monitoring the growing wildfire. She wrote on X that while the fire is burning outside the City of Los Angeles, the LAFD is prepared to respond to any fire threat that could emerge and has predeployed resources across the San Fernando Valley, Santa Monica Mountains, Hollywood Hills, and West LA.
Newsom and Bass faced intense criticism after the devastating Palisades Fire, which began in January 2025 in the Santa Monica Mountains of Los Angeles County and spread to Malibu, which is still recovering from the damage. About 6,845 structures were destroyed and 12 people were killed in that blaze, according to Cal Fire. Bass faced scrutiny over her absence from Los Angeles when the fire erupted and the city fire department's preparedness, while Newsom faced questions about water supplies after firefighters encountered low pressure and dry hydrants.
Former reality TV star Spencer Pratt, who lost his home in the Palisades Fire, later announced a bid for Los Angeles mayor, criticizing state and local leaders over their handling of the disaster. Pratt shared a video of the Bryson Fire on X, writing that with Gavin Newsom in charge, people are on their own. The cause of the Bryson Fire is under investigation.
Henderson Fire and Freeway Reopening
Further south, crews are battling another fast-moving brush fire in Camp Pendleton near Oceanside. The Henderson Fire has burned 1,118 acres since starting just after 2:30 p.m. local time Thursday near the intersection of Henderson and Brown Streets at Camp Pendleton, according to Cal Fire. As of 8 p.m. local time, evacuation orders had been lifted.
The blaze prompted Interstate 5 to close at Basilone Road during the evening commute, but the freeway has since been reopened. The cause of the Henderson Fire also remains under investigation.
